_comment: Failures that are KNOWN and accepted, so the autofix loop does not
re-investigate them every run. Only consulted when verify_all is run
with --baseline; a plain run still reports them as failures, so the
exit code keeps meaning what it always has.
Rules, because an accepted failure is a hole in the gate:
- salient_fingerprint comes from a real run:
- `reason` says what the failure IS and why it is tolerable. Not
'known issue'. Someone reading it in three months has to be able
to decide whether it still applies.
- `expires` is required. An acceptance that cannot age out becomes
permanent by neglect, so verify_all reports an expired entry as a
failure and exits non-zero even when nothing else is wrong.
- If the failure CHANGES, the fingerprint stops matching and the
entry reads 'stale': the recorded reason no longer describes what
is happening, which is reported rather than silently re-accepted.

accepted.reason: B2B-422_get_spendSummary_usermembernotactive_403_suspended loses 1 of 17 steps: `tokenRequest 2`. The case registers no bootstrap, so later calls in it go out unauthenticated. Long-standing and still untraced -- it predates the Round-4 clustering fixes and survived them unchanged. Accepted so the loop works on new failures instead of re-deriving this one. Re-fingerprinted 2026-10-05 after the 14 GOAL suites were converted: the failing case and its unreachable step are byte-identical, and only the inventory line moved (9023 steps/1002 cases -> 9468/1116). The fingerprint covers that line, so ANY growth of the tree invalidates every accepted failure even when nothing about the failure changed -- a weakness in the mechanism, not in this entry. it is NOT fixed, and step-parity is policy `prompt`, so any attempt at it is a deliberate choice at the command line.
accepted.scope: b2b + goal families, 29 suites, 1116 registered cases / 9468 enabled REST steps at time of recording
